day_summary: Bitcoin closed the June 18 UTC day at $62,952.75 — down -2.41% from the June 17 UTC close of $64,509.39 — decisively breaching the $63,500 two-day close stop level that defined the thesis. The full-session range was $62,255.77–$64,814.27, with the high reached early in the session (pre-US open) and BTC selling off steadily through the US afternoon in contrast to the S&P 500 (+1.08%) and Nasdaq (+1.91%) Iran-deal rally. This equity/crypto divergence is the session's defining signal: equities traded the Iran geopolitical relief while BTC traded Fed policy, and those are two very different risks. DXY held at 100.15 despite oil's -5% Brent crash, signaling the Fed hawkish pricing (9/18 dot-plot members projecting 2026 hikes) is more durable than the oil-disinflation trade would suggest. The $62,255.77 intraday low tested a new cycle low for the post-FOMC window, and the UTC midnight close at $62,952.75 confirms Day 1 of the two-day stop clock is TRIGGERED. If BTC closes below $63,500 on the June 19 UTC day (midnight-to-midnight UTC — crypto trades 24/7 through the Juneteenth US holiday), the stop executes and the long position exits. Note: live price at time of this brief generation (01:04 UTC June 19) is $63,093, trending slightly above the UTC close — watch overnight closely.

The Juneteenth weekend introduces maximum adverse-gap risk: thin US ETF desk liquidity, no institutional bid coordination, and macro news (Iran deal progress, Fed speakers) prints into no-bid conditions. Do NOT add any size in this environment. Maintain minimum position until Day 2 resolution. If the stop triggers on June 19, the next re-entry level is $60,000–$62,000 on confirmation of a daily close reclaim — not a knife catch.
